definition_quote.value: The evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, or surgical, nonsurgical, or related treatment of diseases, disorders, or conditions of the eye and its appendages and their impact on the human body provided by an optometrist within the scope of his or her education, training, and experience

methods_authorized.quote: including but not limited to: 1. drug_authority.value: Therapeutically certified optometrists authorized by the board may prescribe oral medications except Schedule I controlled substances and Schedule II controlled substances other than hydrocodone combination products; may prescribe Schedule II hydrocodone combination products and Schedule III-V controlled substances for up to 72-hour supply with no refills; diagnostic agents limited to miotics (emergency), mydriatics, cycloplegics, and topical anesthetics excluding controlled substances.
drug_authority.quote: Any therapeutically certified optometrist licensed under the provisions of this subsection shall be authorized to prescribe oral medications, except any controlled substances classified in Schedule I and any controlled substances classified in Schedule II other than hydrocodone combination products

surgery_prohibited.quote: The following procedures are excluded from the scope of practice of optometry, except for the preoperative and postoperative care of these procedures

surgery_definition.value: Excluded nonlaser and laser surgical procedures include: removal of the eye, full thickness incision/excision of cornea or sclera (other than emergency paracentesis), penetrating/lamellar keratoplasty, incision of iris and ciliary body, incision of vitreous, incision of retina, surgical extraction of crystalline lens, intraocular implants, extraocular muscle surgery, eyelid surgery for malignancies or incisional cosmetic/mechanical repair, bony orbit surgery, lacrimal system incisional/excisional surgery (other than probing), full thickness conjunctivoplasty with graft or flap, any nonlaser surgical procedure not providing correction of ocular abnormalities, injection into posterior chamber for macular/retinal disease, and administration of general anesthesia.
surgery_definition.quote: Nonlaser surgery related to removal of the eye from a living human being; Nonlaser surgery requiring full thickness incision or excision of the cornea or sclera other than paracentesis in an emergency situation

value: Laser surgery procedures excluding retina, LASIK, and PRK are authorized
